property.zoning: B-2 General Business (ESTIMATED - Orange Ave commercial corridor)

Bear Case.narrative: One retail tenant vacates; re-leasing at lower rent. Cap rate expands 150bps.

Base Case.narrative: Stable occupancy with 2% annual rent growth. Cap rate stable at 7.6%.

Bull Case.narrative: Rent growth 3-4% annually, cap rate compresses to 7.0% on market appreciation.

Black Swan.narrative: Anchor grocery tenant defaults. 50% vacancy. Cap rate blows to 10.6%. Land value provides downside floor.

Optimistic / Value-Add.narrative: Reposition residential units, upgrade retail. Cap rate compresses to 6.5%. ~$150K renovation investment.

Location / Barriers.rationale: Orange Ave is Irvington primary corridor. Walk Score 80/100. Good visibility, corner lot. BUT: Irvington is a challenged submarket within Tier 1 Essex County. Limited barriers to entry. New construction can compete. Zoning allows similar development nearby.

Tenant Quality.rationale: Grocery anchor on 7-year lease provides some stability. But 4 of 5 units on YTY leases. Tenants are local small businesses, not credit-rated. Residential tenants easily replaceable. 100% occupancy masks lease duration fragility.

Asset Quality.rationale: Class C building, 1948 construction. Renovated 2013 and refreshed 2025. 3 parking spaces only (0.57/1,000 SF - low). 2-story walkup. Functional but not premium. FAR 1.24 means some development upside.

Market Position.rationale: Corner location with street frontage on Orange Ave. Mixed-use format serves neighborhood needs. BUT: Competing retail on same corridor. No dominant market position. Small property ($800K) means limited institutional interest = less competition for this size.

Cash Flow Stability.rationale: 100% leased, in-place income. 5 diverse tenants (grocery, services, residential) = diversification. $94,992 gross with $60,882 NOI = 64% margin. 7.6% cap is healthy for Class C. BUT: YTY leases mean cash flow can shift quickly. Grocery is 7yr anchor but small tenant risk.

Value-Add / Optionality.rationale: FAR 1.24 on 0.10 AC lot = some development upside (could add density). 2025 renovation means capex needs are low near-term. Residential units could be upgraded for rent growth. Corner lot = potential for redevelopment long-term. Separate utilities = easy to bill back.

risks.detail: Grocery store on 7-year lease is ~40-50% of rent roll. If they fail, NOI could drop 35-50%. Finding replacement grocery tenant for Class C space is difficult. Personal guarantee strength unknown.
risks.mitigant: Verify lease guarantees. Request tenant financials. Negotiate security deposit equal to 3-6 months rent.

risks.detail: 4 of 5 units on year-to-year leases. Simultaneous non-renewal could create 60-80% vacancy. Re-leasing costs and downtime would compress NOI significantly.
risks.mitigant: Incentivize conversion to 2-3 year leases post-acquisition. Build $15K vacancy reserve.

risks.detail: Irvington has higher crime rates and lower median income than Essex County average. Any further deterioration could depress rents and cap rates.
risks.mitigant: Orange Ave corridor is designated for revitalization. NJ Transit access provides floor. Low price point ($800K) limits absolute downside.

risks.detail: 1948 building. Even with 2013/2025 renovations, Class C assets carry hidden issues: roof, HVAC, plumbing, electrical. Inspection may reveal $30-75K in near-term capex.
risks.mitigant: Thorough property condition assessment. Budget $25K reserve for year 1-2 capex.

risks.detail: Sale at $800K vs assessment of $427K triggers reassessment risk. If reassessed to ~$800K at 4% rate, taxes jump from ~$17,092 to ~$32,000 - an increase that could consume ~$15K of NOI annually.
risks.mitigant: Model post-acquisition tax at 80-100% of purchase price. Appeal if assessment exceeds market.

risks.detail: Convenience store/grocery may have underground storage tanks or dry cleaning history. 1948 construction = potential asbestos, lead paint.
risks.mitigant: Phase I ESA recommended. Budget $3-5K for environmental due diligence.

risks.detail: Small Class C mixed-use in Irvington has limited buyer pool. Exit may take 6-12 months. Financing-dependent buyers may struggle with rate environment.
risks.mitigant: Price at entry provides margin of safety. 7.6% cap rate is attractive to cash buyers. Seller financing could expand buyer pool on exit.
